Encode a JWT

Source: R/jwt.R
jwt_encode.Rd

jwt_encode() signs a claims set as a JSON Web Token (RFC 7519), in the compact serialization.

Usage

jwt_encode(
  claims,
  key,
  alg = NULL,
  header = list(typ = "JWT"),
  expires_in = NULL,
  not_before = NULL,
  issued_at = TRUE,
  jti = FALSE
)

Arguments

claims

The claims, as a named list. It may be empty.

key

A jwk, or a list of jws_signer() objects for several signatures.

alg

The signature algorithm, such as "HS256" or "RS256". NULL takes the key's own alg.

header

Protected header members. The default declares typ: "JWT".

expires_in

Seconds, or a difftime, until the token expires. Sets exp.

not_before

Seconds, or a difftime, before the token becomes valid. Sets nbf.

issued_at

Whether to set iat to now, unless claims sets it.

jti

Whether to add a random jti, 128 bits from the operating system's random source as Base64url, unless claims sets it.

Value

The JWT, as a single string.

Details

Times may be given as POSIXct for exp, nbf and iat, and are written as NumericDate, whole seconds since 1970. expires_in and not_before count from now.

See also

jwt_decode() to check one.

Examples

key <- jwk_oct(as.raw(1:32), kid = "k1")
jwt <- jwt_encode(list(sub = "u1", aud = "api"), key, "HS256",
                       expires_in = 3600)
jwt_decode(jwt, key, algorithms = "HS256", audience = "api")
#> <jwt_claims> verified HS256, key "k1"
#>   sub: "u1"
#>   aud: "api"
#>   exp: 2026-11-03 14:03:14 UTC
#>   iat: 2026-11-03 13:03:14 UTC
